result.name: Kitchen wall panel with a long name

result.label: Panel ID
result.help: Stable id used in entity IDs (lowercase, digits, underscores; 63 characters maximum).
result.summary: Stable id used in this panel's entity IDs.

result.label: Friendly name
result.summary: Name Home Assistant shows for this panel.

result.label: Manufacturer
result.help: HA device-card manufacturer override (blank = profile/auto).
result.summary: Override the manufacturer on the Home Assistant device card.

result.label: Model
result.help: HA device-card model override (blank = profile/auto).
result.summary: Override the model on the Home Assistant device card.

result.label: Area in Home Assistant
result.help: Where this panel lives, by Home Assistant area name. This can only be changed in Panel Assistant if your HA user has admin permissions, otherwise change it on your device in HA.
result.summary: Home Assistant area this panel belongs to.

result.label: Auto-sleep activity source
result.help:
Use the panel’s calibrated proximity sensor, Home Assistant Area devices, or touch inactivity.

- Presence modes pause if their source is unavailable.
- Touch inactivity needs no presence setup.
result.summary: What counts as presence: proximity sensor, area or touch.

result.label: Touch inactivity delay (seconds)
result.help: When Touch inactivity is selected, switch the screen fully off after this many seconds without a touch.
result.summary: Seconds without a touch before the screen goes off.

result.label: Auto sleep
result.help: Switch the screen off after the selected presence mode’s learned delay or the chosen touch inactivity delay. Manual screen control remains separate.
result.summary: Turn the screen off when nobody is around or after inactivity.

result.label: Navbar mode
result.help:
Soft on-screen navigation bar for panels with no native navbar. **Native** leaves navigation to the panel's own Android bar and draws nothing.

Hiding the Android system bars, from the built-in renderer's fullscreen setting or the Android dashboard lock, still hides a native bar.
result.summary: Show a soft navigation bar on panels without a native one.

result.label: Wake on wave
result.help: Wake after a calibrated clear-to-near-to-clear wave. Set up proximity on the panel; touch-to-wake remains available.
result.summary: Wave a hand near the panel to wake it.

result.label: Lock Android to dashboard (experimental)
result.help:
Root-only casual-use lock. Hides Android system bars and returns to the selected dashboard within about 3 seconds when another app or Recents opens. It does not hide Home Assistant navigation.

Release it:

- here, or from Home Assistant
- through adb
- with 7 rapid top-left taps
- during the 60-second unlocked window after reboot
result.summary: Root only. Bring the dashboard back when another app opens.

result.label: App watchdog
result.summary: Relaunch the dashboard app if it dies or stays backgrounded.

result.label: Touch sound
result.summary: Play the system tap sound.

result.label: Silence boot chime
result.summary: Mute the firmware start-up chime.

result.label: Dark mode
result.help:
Themes Panel Assistant's own screens and sets the dashboard's default colour scheme on panels without a system dark-mode setting (Android 9 and older).

A theme picked inside Home Assistant overrides the dashboard default; this web UI always follows the viewing browser's own preference.
result.summary: Dark theme for Panel Assistant's own screens and the dashboard default.

result.label: Ambient light source
result.help: Blank uses the panel light sensor. Select a Home Assistant illuminance sensor when the panel has no suitable sensor.
result.summary: Use a Home Assistant light sensor instead of the panel's.

result.label: Show network warning on dashboard
result.help: Show the network connection warning on this panel's dashboard. Network checks and status remain available when this is off.
result.summary: Warn on the dashboard when the network drops.

result.label: Auto-brightness
result.help: On-panel engine maps a lux stream to the backlight (off = HA drives the screen).
result.summary: Let the panel set the backlight from ambient light.

result.label: Minimum level
result.help: Lowest automatic screen level as a percentage. Proposals scale between the minimum and maximum; manual brightness can still go lower.
result.summary: Lowest level auto-brightness will choose.

result.label: Maximum level
result.help: Highest automatic screen level as a percentage. Proposals scale between the minimum and maximum; manual brightness can still go higher.
result.summary: Highest level auto-brightness will choose.

result.label: CPU profile
result.help: Live CPU scaling profile until reboot; Auto = the SoC's dynamic governor.
result.summary: CPU scaling profile until the next reboot.

result.label: Zigbee router
result.summary: Use the on-board Zigbee radio as a router.

result.label: Prevent idle dim
result.summary: Stop the vendor firmware dimming the backlight at screen-off.

result.label: Keep panel responsive
result.summary: Keep network and services running while the screen is off.

result.label: Camera
result.help: Off by default. Serves RTSP video with room audio where a microphone is available and permitted, and JPEG snapshots for Home Assistant. Capture starts only when a client requests media, and the panel shows a red light while the camera is open.
result.summary: Serve the panel camera as an RTSP stream and JPEG snapshot.

result.label: Resolution
result.help: What a stream gets when its URL does not ask for something else. A stream URL can override it with ?res=, in either direction.
result.summary: Default stream resolution; a stream URL can override it.

result.label: Frame rate
result.help: What a stream gets when its URL does not ask for something else. A stream URL can override it with ?fps=, in either direction.
result.summary: Default frame rate; a stream URL can override it.

result.label: Bitrate (kbps)
result.help: What a stream gets when its URL does not ask for something else. A stream URL can override it with ?kbps=, in either direction.
result.summary: Default bitrate; a stream URL can override it.

result.label: Exposure
result.help: Exposure bias in stops, for a camera that reads a room darker or brighter than it looks. 0 leaves the camera's own automatic exposure alone; the panel clamps this to whatever range the sensor actually supports.
result.summary: Exposure bias in stops. 0 leaves auto exposure alone.

result.label: Dashboard app
result.summary: App that shows the dashboard. Blank uses the built-in renderer.

result.label: Entity filtering
result.help: Built-in renderer: limit Home Assistant's state stream to dashboard-used entities and learn runtime dependencies. Manage sources and pins in Entities.
result.summary: Only stream the entities this dashboard uses.

result.label: Home dashboard
result.help:
Dashboard used by reload and idle return.

- **Auto** lets Home Assistant choose.
- **Custom** accepts a specific view, e.g. `/dashboard-name/tab-name`.
result.summary: Dashboard opened on reload and idle return.

result.label: Dashboard theme
result.help:
Built-in renderer only.

- **Follow Home Assistant** leaves the dashboard's light/dark choice to Home Assistant, which is what the Dark mode setting supplies a default for.
- **Dark** and **Light** choose it on this panel when Home Assistant is set to Auto, for a kiosk dashboard with no sidebar to reach the Home Assistant profile page from.
- **Ambient** chooses Dark or Light from the room's light as the auto-brightness model sees it, and changes only after the room has stayed darker or lighter for a minute; it needs Auto-brightness on, and follows Home Assistant until it has a reading.

An explicit Light or Dark choice in Home Assistant still wins; use Auto or a separate panel user. Returning to Follow Home Assistant hands the choice back exactly as it was found.
result.summary: Who picks light or dark: Home Assistant, this panel or the room.

result.label: Hide Android system bars
result.help:
Built-in renderer only. Hides Android's status and navigation bars while the dashboard is in front; swipe from an edge to reveal them temporarily.

It does not lock the panel or hide Home Assistant navigation.
result.summary: Hide Android's status and navigation bars behind the dashboard.

result.label: Hide Home Assistant navigation (native)
result.help:
Built-in renderer only. After Home Assistant 2026.4.2+ connects, asks its native frontend to hide its navigation.

On by default; an unsupported or failed request leaves the dashboard unchanged. It does not lock Android or inject CSS into the dashboard.
result.summary: Ask Home Assistant to hide its own navigation.

result.label: Idle return to home (min)
result.summary: Minutes idle before returning home. 0 turns it off.

result.label: Home Assistant URL
result.help: Built-in renderer: Home Assistant base URL, e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123. Blank disables it.
result.summary: Address of your Home Assistant server.

result.label: Long-lived access token
result.help: Use browser sign-in when possible. This fallback can be created in your Home Assistant user profile.
result.summary: Fallback token when browser sign-in is not possible.

result.label: Zoom (%)
result.help: Browser zoom.
result.summary: Browser zoom for the dashboard.

result.label: Interface language
result.help:
Language used by Panel Assistant's own interface.

**Automatic** uses an explicit page override first. Configure setting labels and help can then follow the connected Home Assistant user's language; browser, device and English are the remaining fallbacks.
result.summary: Language of Panel Assistant's own interface.

result.label: Launcher app
result.help: App the Launcher button brings forward. Blank auto-picks an app. Selecting Panel launcher (Panel Assistant) also makes and keeps Panel Assistant the Android Home app.
result.summary: App the Launcher button opens.

result.label: Network ADB
result.help:
**Security risk:** keeps classic ADB listening on TCP port 5555 across boots and reconnects.

Enable only during active maintenance on a trusted network. If ADB was enabled outside Panel Assistant, it must also be disabled there.
result.summary: Security risk. Keep ADB listening on port 5555 across boots.

result.label: Voice assistant
result.summary: Listen for a wake word and send speech to Assist.

result.label: Wake words
result.help: The wake words to listen for: the bundled Okay Nabu, Hey Jarvis, Hey Mycroft and Alexa, and any you import below.
result.summary: Wake words to listen for.

result.label: Wake word pipelines
result.help: Which Home Assistant Assist pipeline each wake word runs. A wake word left on the preferred pipeline follows whichever pipeline Home Assistant prefers.
result.summary: Which Assist pipeline each wake word runs.

result.label: Audio source
result.summary: Android audio source for the listener.

result.label: Wake sensitivity
result.help:
Wake-word detector threshold, applied as an offset to the model's cutoff score.

- **Low** requires a clearer match: fewer false wakes, more likely to miss a quiet or distant call.
- **Normal** applies no offset.
- **High** matches more readily: faster to wake, more false triggers.
result.summary: How readily the wake word triggers.

result.label: Microphone gain (dB)
result.help:
Amplifies the audio sent to Home Assistant for transcription.

These panels expose no platform noise suppression or automatic gain control, so a panel heard from across the room may wake reliably and still transcribe poorly: wake-word detection adapts to a quiet signal on its own and speech-to-text does not.

**Raise this** if commands are missed or mistranscribed while the wake word works. Wake-word detection is deliberately left on the unamplified signal.
result.summary: Amplify speech sent to Home Assistant for transcription.

result.label: Ship logs
result.help: Forward Panel Assistant's own process log — not the full system log — to a central sink (LAN-only, tokens and passwords redacted).
result.summary: Send Panel Assistant's own log to a collector on your network.

result.label: Ship system logs
result.help:
Forward Android system logs to the same sink when Ship logs is on.

- Off by default.
- Requires TCP or HTTP, and root or the installed helper.
- Entries are redacted; high-volume output may be dropped.
result.summary: Also send Android system logs to the collector.

result.label: Sink host
result.help: Log-collector host; blank keeps shipping inert. A scheme or :port here is honoured (udp://collector, collector:1514).
result.summary: Log collector address. Blank turns shipping off.

result.label: Sink port
result.summary: Log collector port.

result.label: Protocol
result.help: TCP is the default because it reports a sink that is refusing or unreachable; UDP cannot, so a wrong setting there fails silently. Port 514 serves both.
result.summary: Transport to the collector. TCP reports a refused sink.

result.label: Screen brightness
result.help: Current screen state and brightness. Home Assistant presents the light's native 0–255 brightness as a percentage.
result.summary: Screen state and brightness.

result.label: Panel volume
result.help: Current panel media volume reported on its native 0–100 percent scale.
result.summary: Panel media volume.

result.label: Ambient light
result.summary: Ambient light from the panel sensor.

result.label: Proximity
result.summary: Learned near or far occupancy.

result.label: Proximity level
result.help: Normalized learned proximity level from 0 to 100 percent; binary sources report 0 or 100.
result.summary: Learned proximity level, 0 to 100 percent.

result.label: Auto-sleep activity
result.help: Whether the auto-sleep policy is currently holding the panel awake. The Home Assistant entity provides the activity history timeline.
result.summary: Whether auto-sleep is holding the panel awake.

result.label: Temperature
result.summary: Temperature from Android's panel sensor.

result.label: Humidity
result.summary: Humidity from Android's panel sensor.

result.label: IP address
result.summary: This panel's local IPv4 address.

result.label: CPU usage
result.help: Overall CPU busy percentage (root/su panels; unavailable on sandbox-walled panels).
result.summary: Overall CPU busy percentage.

result.label: Memory usage
result.summary: Used memory as a percentage.

result.label: SoC temperature
result.help: System-on-chip temperature (root/su panels; unavailable on sandbox-walled panels).
result.summary: Processor temperature.

result.label: Last boot time
result.help: When the panel last booted (a timestamp — HA shows the elapsed uptime).
result.summary: When the panel last started.

result.label: Wi-Fi network
result.help: Current Wi-Fi network name while Wi-Fi is the active connection. This can identify a location and enters HA history when exposed; Android may hide it unless network-information permission is available.
result.summary: Current Wi-Fi network name.

result.label: Wi-Fi signal strength
result.help: Current Wi-Fi received signal strength in dBm while Wi-Fi is the active connection.
result.summary: Current Wi-Fi signal strength.

result.label: Wi-Fi outages (24 h)
result.help: Short Wi-Fi dropouts in the rolling last 24 hours. Counts loss of the panel's active Wi-Fi connection only — Home Assistant outages are never counted. If the panel had to cap what it stores, the sensor's is_lower_bound attribute says the value is a floor.
result.summary: Short Wi-Fi dropouts in the last 24 hours.

result.label: Room temperature
result.help: Room air temperature from the panel's supported climate sensor (calibration offset applied).
result.summary: Room temperature from the climate sensor.

result.label: Room humidity
result.summary: Room humidity from the climate sensor.

result.label: Room temperature offset
result.help: Correction (°C) added to the reported room temperature — usually negative, since panel self-heating reads high. Per-panel (depends on mounting), so not cloned by a fleet push.
result.summary: Correction added to the room temperature, in °C.
